dedupe_keys.name: salus system approach to land use sustainability crop soil water and nutrient model

description: SALUS is a process-based model that simulates crop, soil, water and nutrient conditions day by day over many years under different management strategies. The Michigan State University project page says a run can include crop rotations, planting dates, plant populations, irrigation and fertiliser applications and tillage, for any period with weather data, and that several strategies can run side by side under the same weather to compare their effects. Each day it runs components for management, water balance, soil organic matter, nitrogen and phosphorus dynamics, heat balance, and plant growth and development. The water balance covers runoff, infiltration, evaporation, saturated and unsaturated flow, drainage, root uptake and transpiration, and growth is limited by water and nitrogen. The lab's tools page offers the input and output data structure (with a PDF), soil layer rules, soil water limit and texture programs, global variables, and gridded NLDAS-2 and GRIDMET weather in SALUS format. Access, licence, source code and versioning are not stated on the pages read. Coverage is any site with weather and soil data. Caveats: field-scale model; download terms must be asked of the lab. For simulation it estimates yield losses and irrigation and fertiliser demand under drought, heat or management change. Related catalogue records include DSSAT, APSIM and STICS.
